thread.title: Stock Market Gains Fade; Small Caps Still Lead Stock Market Gains Fade As Small Caps Lead Hesitant Advance | Investor's Business Daily

author: JUAN CARLOS ARANCIBIA
title: Stock Market Gains Fade; Small Caps Still Lead Stock Market Gains Fade As Small Caps Lead Hesitant Advance | Investor's Business Daily
text:
The stock market remained unsettled as the major indexes sharply pared gains of more than 1% and were trying to save modest gains.
X Small caps led, with the Russell 2000 up 1.1%.
The Nasdaq composite had less than 0.1% left of what was a gain exceeding 1%. The S&P 500 rose 0.2% after it too gave up most of a 1%-plus gain. The Dow Jones industrial average added 0.4%.
On the Dow, Verizon ( VZ ) looked strong, up 3% and now extended from a 55.31 buy point. The stock has been in IBD Leaderboard since Oct. 10. Walmart ( WMT ) is following through on a breakout from a 100.31 buy point that occurred Monday.
Apple ( AAPL ) was nearly unchanged after the company unveiled new iPads and Mac computers at an event in New York. The stock is trending below its 50-day moving average.
Volume was tracking higher on the NYSE and Nasdaq compared with the same time Monday. Advancers led decliners by a 3-2 ratio on the NYSE and Nasdaq.
Building-related groups rose, including homebuilders. The beaten-up group rose more than 3% but remains at almost the lowest ranking of 197 groups.
Consumer stocks also were in favor, with home furnishings, apparel chains, consumer electronics and apparel manufacturers up more than 3%.
Real estate investment trusts — more appealing now because of their dividends — continue to act well. Simon Property ( SPG ) broke out of a base with a 188.13 buy point. The relative strength line made a new high and volume was well above average, two positive signs. Citigroup raised the price target on Simon Property shares to 200 from 190 and maintained a buy rating.
Earnings reports were behind some of the day's biggest declines.
Texas Roadhouse ( TXRH ) gapped down below its 200-day moving average in heavy trading. The restaurant chain missed profit expectations late Monday.
Wingstop ( WING ) was a bit volatile but nearly flat Tuesday afternoon following its earnings report, which beat expectations. Wingstop is trading below its 50-day moving average but is not in a sell situation.
